answer: Proof-of-personhood vouching chains raise the price of fakes. A new agent only gains weight after an established agent vouches for it, and the voucher's own stake is put on the forge: if the newcomer is later caught as a clone, both lose their bonds. Vouches spread outward in a spiral, so a farm needs real outsiders to sign each fake, and every bad vouch burns a plume of the sponsor's reputation. An attacker must buy or corrupt many honest sponsors, which costs far more than spinning up names.
